title: second-shift consumer-repo configuration (static context)
description: The single per-repo onboarding file (.claude/second-shift.config.json). Everything repo-specific that the generic plugins need: tracker, topology, base branches, command truth table, reviewer registry deltas, paths, gates. Domain knowledge does NOT belong here — it lives in repo-local skills and extension files (see docs/extension-points.md).

$schema.description: Optional editor-validation pointer; onboard writes the schema URL at the pinned marketplace ref.

configVersion.description: Schema version of this config file; bumped only on breaking schema changes.

writes.description: Whether the pipeline writes back to the tracker (comments, status/label transitions, claim). github default true (queue+claim+comment model); JIRA setups typically run read-only (fetch the ticket via MCP, never transition or comment — the state file + draft-PR metadata are the audit trail), so JIRA repos usually set false. A false value makes the tracker-write steps no-ops; ticket fetch stays active regardless.

branchPrefix.description: Branch-name namespace prepended to the ticket key. The work branch is "<branchPrefix><ticketKey>". github example: "claude/acme-" (→ claude/acme-42). JIRA example: a per-user identifier plus a slash, e.g. "jdoe/" (→ jdoe/gh-540).

bot.description: Dedicated bot identity for the pipeline's GitHub writes: PR comments and markers, the git committer, and — under tracker.type github only — the claim. Legal under either tracker.type, because source control is GitHub for every adapter, so a JIRA-tracked repo writes to GitHub too and needs the identity just as much. The key sits under `tracker` for historical reasons; its scope is the code host.

wrapperPath.description: Explicit path to the gh-as-bot wrapper script. When set, install-gh-bot.sh writes it here and claim-issue.sh's GH_BOT default resolves to it, instead of the $HOME/.config/<repo-basename>/gh-as-bot.sh derivation (which was derived wrong once — a canary catch). Supports $HOME/~ expansion.

app.description: GitHub App identity for the bot (previously hardcoded in install-gh-bot.sh with no config home). Onboarding a different repo's bot app sets these instead of editing script constants.

appName.description: GitHub App slug, e.g. "acme-dev-pipeline" (used in settings-page URLs and messages).

privateKeyFilename.description: Private-key filename installed under the bot config dir, e.g. "acme-dev-pipeline.private-key.pem".

installationId.description: Optional: pin the installation ID to skip API discovery.

keyPattern.description: Regex for ticket keys as used in branch names and record filenames (e.g. "[A-Z]+-[0-9]+" for JIRA, "[0-9]+" for GitHub issue numbers). Read by preflight.sh (which reports the effective pattern) and retro-corpus.sh (which filters the run corpus by it); predecessor-gate.sh applies the same pattern from its caller. Absent = accept any non-empty key.

labels.description: github only: the queue/claim/blocker label vocabulary by ROLE (not a flat list). Every functional site reads these roles — the queue-label confirm at build-lean step 1, the claim label-swap, the do-not-pick-up guard, claim-issue.sh, and pipeline-doctor — and the pre-flight existence check verifies their union. Absent → the shipped defaults. Config home for the previously-hardcoded label literals (F75); a consumer with custom labels sets these once and every site follows.

queue.description: The label the pipeline picks work from and drops at claim. A crashed claim swap can leave it behind, so the unclaim workflow /second-shift:onboard emits also releases it when the item CLOSES. Default "ready-for-dev".

claimed.description: The label added atomically at claim. It stays on for as long as the work is in flight — including through review, since the lean lane's exit milestone still requires an OPEN pr — and is released when the tracker item CLOSES, by the unclaim workflow /second-shift:onboard emits. Default "in-progress".

blockers.description: Labels that block auto-pickup (an issue carrying any is skipped). Default ["epic","needs-intake-review","needs-spec-work","needs-plan-review"].

repos.description: Keyed by logical repo id ("be", "fe", or a single id for standalone/monorepo). The pipeline is always invoked from the repo this config lives in; sibling repos are reached via relative paths.

path.description: Relative to the config's repo root; "." for the host repo.

baseBranch.description: The integration mainline PRs target (repos in a pair may differ, e.g. BE alpha / FE main).

worktreesDir.description: Where pipeline worktrees are created for this repo (default ../<repo>-worktrees).

ticketTag.description: Ticket-title tag routing work to this repo (e.g. "[BE]"). No lane gates on it: the lean lane (/dev-pipeline:run-lean) treats it as advisory routing for whoever launches the session, read by the intake-orchestrator skill as ticket-filing policy. The staged lane that read it as a gate input was deleted in #348.

commands.description: Command truth table per logical repo id (keys must exist in topology.repos). null = lane not available in this repo; lean-gate.sh milestone 3 and preflight.sh both skip a null lane rather than inventing one.

lintAutofixes.description: Whether the lint command mutates files. preflight.sh skips the lint lane when this is true — a read-only pre-flight never runs a mutating command — and LINT_AUTOFIX is the lane's class in the closed failure taxonomy.

allowUnverified.description: Zero-lane safety valve. When no verifying lane is configured (lint/typecheck/test all null and extraLanes empty), preflight.sh withholds its pipeline-ready verdict and lean-gate.sh milestone 3 reds naming the opt-out — unless this is true, which declares the opt-out deliberate. Inert when any verifying lane is configured.

lanes.description: SETUP-ONLY steps run sequentially BEFORE the built-in lint/typecheck/test trio (e.g. dependency install, workspace-package builds for apps/*, packages/*). Every lane failure is classed INFRA (environment/setup), NOT a code defect — a lane never gets the TEST_FAILURE/TYPE_ERROR fix budget. Do NOT put a test/lint/typecheck command here (e.g. `poetry run pytest`): its failures would be misreported as environment errors and bypass the fix budget. For additive VERIFY-style lanes that carry a real failure class and the standard fix budget, use extraLanes (EP-2) below.

extraLanes.description: EP-2: additive verify lanes. Run sequentially AFTER the built-in SUITE lanes, never interleaving or replacing them. Results land under namespaced ext:<name> keys in the verify summary (canonical keys unreachable). No advisory mode — a lane blocks lean-gate.sh milestone 3 or it does not exist.

name.description: kebab-case, unique; results recorded under ext:<name>.

when.description: Changed-file globs gating execution; empty/absent = always run. Skip/inert-diff behavior is the consuming lane's own.

failureClass.description: MUST be an existing closed failure-taxonomy value — extensions borrow the taxonomy, never extend it. Blocking; the attempt-budget behavior belongs to the consuming lane (lean-gate's 3-attempt milestone budget).

reviewers.description: Deltas against the plugin-shipped review-lead registry.

add.description: Repo-local reviewer agents (in this repo's .claude/agents/) to register with review-lead.

dimensions.description: Review dimensions this agent covers (dedup/routing hint for review-lead).

remove.description: Plugin-shipped reviewers to disable in this repo (e.g. db-reviewer in an FE repo).

modelOverrides.description: Per-agent model-tier override, keyed by any agent the .mjs dispatch tables model — the review-lead panel reviewers, the intake fan-out agents, and the structured-emitter transcription sink (EP-4; the named mutation-executor override left with its engine, #574). Observed need: security-reviewer opus in one repo, sonnet in another. check-model-tiers validates .mjs tables against frontmatter + these overrides. Values must be tiers this consumer's subscription can actually dispatch — an inaccessible tier surfaces as a dead reviewer and the gate fails closed. `fable` is override-only: never a shipped default, and a check-model-tiers error if it appears in a shipped dispatch table.

additionalProperties.description: A dispatch model (haiku, sonnet, opus, fable) OR a tier name from the effective reviewers.tierMap. That union is a cross-field constraint JSON Schema cannot express — it depends on a sibling property — so this half asserts only "string" and config-lint.sh carries the real check, including typo detection. Do not re-add an enum here: it would reject every legal tier name.

tierMap.description: Retarget an abstract tier to a different dispatch model (#351). MERGES per tier over the plugin-shipped alphabet in dev-pipeline's model-tiering.md, so a config naming one tier leaves the rest at their defaults and a config naming none dispatches exactly as it did before this key existed. This is the vendor-independence seam: shipped dispatch tables name tiers rather than vendor tokens, so a consumer whose subscription lacks a model class retargets it here instead of forking the plugin. Additive and optional, so configVersion stays at 2.

plansDir.description: Directory (worktree-relative) holding the lane's per-ticket records — the spec/AC file, the review verdict record, and the design render receipt. Default = the plugin's current literal; a consumer that sets it has it honored. Read by lean-gate.sh (which resolves every milestone artifact under it), lean-reconcile.sh and retro-corpus.sh.

gates.description: Optional pipeline gates/capabilities. Everything defaults to off; a gate that is on but missing its prerequisites must fail closed at run time.

mutation.description: false declares the mutation seam deliberately off (an explicit off-switch a reader can see, as opposed to the silent absence of a sweep). Absent/true = the seam is expected. The lean lane's sweep is repo-carried — lean-gate.sh milestone 3 runs tools/mutation-sweep.sh when the repo ships one and records SKIPPED when it does not — so this key is the declared INTENT that onboard's config-grill grades that plumbing against, not a switch the gate reads.

design.description: Optional design-fidelity axis. Selects the design-toolkit adapter family. Key absent = design fidelity off (a run behaves exactly as a non-design run). Prerequisites missing at run time (Figma MCP for figma; DesignSync for claude-design) fail closed, same posture as every gate.

provider.description: figma → figma-faithful skills + Figma-MCP prerequisite; claude-design → design-faithful skills + DesignSync prerequisite.

liveRender.description: Arms a repo-owned render command on build-lean milestone 3. Config alone arms nothing: the gate additionally requires a per-ticket `## Design` section in the committed spec, and once a ticket arms, the disarm state-locks. Failure is BLOCKING on the run's shared 3-attempt fix budget, with no degraded state — the milestone renders every RS row, hashes them into a committed receipt, and reds until that receipt is committed. See docs/live-render.md.

command.description: Repo-owned render script with {route} and {out} placeholders, plus an optional {state} the lean lane substitutes, e.g. "yarn render:verify --route {route} --state {state} --out {out}". {route} is the app-relative leaf below the feature mount path (the harness owns any shell/org prefix); {state} is the render state named by a lean spec's | RS-n | row, and is REQUIRED in the template whenever a ticket declares a state other than `default`; the harness owns boot/auth/screenshot and must emit a PNG at {out}, exiting nonzero with a clear message on failure. Placeholders must appear UNQUOTED — the lean gate shell-quotes each substituted value. See docs/live-render.md.

cwd.description: Topology repo id (topology.repos key) whose checkout the command runs in. Default: the fe repo when the topology has one, else the sole repo. The gate resolves it to the ticket's worktree, never the main checkout.

readyProbe.description: Optional URL curl-checked before spawning the command (e.g. a sibling BE health endpoint). Probe failure degrades fast with the probe detail instead of waiting out the render timeout.

stageParams.description: Optional stage-prose constants promoted to config. Every key is optional and defaults to the plugin's current shipped literal, so an empty config reproduces today's behavior byte-for-byte. Pure parameterization — no ordering, no logic.

planFilePattern.description: Plan file path pattern. Tokens: {plansDir} (from paths.plansDir), {issueKey}. Unknown tokens are stripped defensively at substitution time.

requiredLabels.description: Tracker labels the queue-and-claim model requires. Default = the plugin's shipped set (ready-for-dev, needs-spec-work, needs-plan-review, needs-intake-review, in-progress, epic).

webComponentGlobs.description: The web-component surface: the globs whose presence in the diff route the a11y reviewer and the design-fidelity reviewer (read by review-lead when it selects the panel). Set this when the FE is not React-under-apps/web — e.g. ["src/app/**/*.{html,ts}"] (Angular), ["src/**/*.vue"] (Vue), ["app/**/*.tsx"] (React Router v7).

inertPattern.description: INERT-lane classifier override, read by tools/is-inert-diff.sh and tools/preflight.sh: an extended regular expression that REPLACES the shipped inert set outright. Omit to keep the default, which is JS/TS-centric — it treats *.md, *.sh, .github/workflows/*.yml and .claude/** data files as inert because a JS/TS lint/type-check/test suite gives them zero coverage. Set this when your product surface IS one of those extensions: on a shell-and-Markdown repo the default classifies every real diff inert, so the configured lint/test lanes never run and the green gate reports a false green. Replace-not-merge is deliberate — only replacement can REMOVE an alternative such as \.sh$; the value is a hand-copy and will not inherit future additions to the default. An uncompilable pattern is rejected by config-lint, and fails closed to the full suite at runtime.

grillWaivers.description: Declared opt-outs for config-grill findings — the checker /second-shift:onboard runs on its draft and /second-shift:doctor runs on the committed config, which reports a capability that is detectably OFF. config-lint cannot see any of it: absence is legal for every optional key, so a structural validator never touches the tree. Keys are CHECK IDS, carrying the repo id wherever the check is per-repo (e.g. "T4.mutation-plumbing.api"): a dotted config path would silence two distinct checks that share a key, and a bare check id would silence every repo under a multi-repo topology. The value is the human-authored reason — never synthesized by a tool. Same shape as commands.<repo>.allowUnverified: a deliberate declared opt-out, visible in a reviewable diff. Additive and optional, so configVersion stays at 2.
